transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-18
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Alice Chen (Redwood AE), Mark Patel (Redwood SE), Emma Rogers (Head of ML, Nova), Daniel Kim (CTO, Nova), Priya Rao (SecOps, Nova)

Summary: quick scoping for a 6-week POC validating Redwood inference for Nova's claim-triage microservice. Focus on SLOs, cost, security and milestones.

[00:00] Alice Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alice, AE on the account. With me is Mark, our solutions engineer. How are you all?
[00:12] Emma Rogers: Hey Alice, doing well. Thanks. Excited to get this scoped. We ya, we're under pressure to pick a vendor by early Q1.
[00:20] Daniel Kim: Hi, Daniel here, quick note on time box: we want to validate both latency and regulatory fidelity.
[00:28] Mark Patel: Cool. We'll focus the POC around those. Quick agenda: confirm success criteria, understand workload sizing, agree benchmark plan, and lock milestones.
[00:35] Priya Rao: Also security access steps — VPC peering and KMS. We'll need clarity there.
[00:40] Alice Chen: Absolutely. First, success criteria — what would a successful POC look like for Nova?
[00:50] Emma Rogers: For us success is three-fold: 1) latency — p95 under 150ms for single-turn triage requests, 2) cost no more than ~0.8x current infra spend per 1k requests, and 3) outputs match our regulatory prompts — we need >=95% correctness on redaction/flagging rules.
[01:15] Mark Patel: Got it. When you say 150ms p95, is that including network egress, or pure inference?
[01:22] Daniel Kim: We're measuring from our service-to-service call — so includes network. We'll provide the region details.
[01:30] Mark Patel: Good to know — we'll include a network realistic measurement. We'll also run both hosted Redwood API and a dedicated deployment if you want to see tradeoffs.
[01:41] Emma Rogers: We'd like a Dedicated env for the POC if possible — because isolation matters for compliance.
[01:47] Priya Rao: Yes, Dedicated or Private (VPC) — needs KMS integration; keys must be customer-managed.
[01:54] Alice Chen: Understood. We can provision a dedicated pool for the POC and we support external KMS/HSM. We'll capture the KMS details in the security pack we'll share.
[02:05] Mark Patel: On workload sizing — can you walk us through expected throughput and concurrency?
[02:12] Daniel Kim: Baseline is around 50k calls/month for the triage endpoint, peak concurrency around 150-250 concurrent requests during business hours. Most request lengths under 1k tokens.
[02:24] Emma Rogers: Also note 30% of requests include attachments (images) but for this POC we'll scope to text-only first.
[02:33] Mark Patel: That's fine; we'll start with text to reduce variables. For 200 concurrent and those token sizes, we'll recommend a 3-GPU dedicated pool with autoscale burst so you can hit p95 targets. We'll include cost estimates in the SOW.
[02:48] Alice Chen: On benchmarks — we'll need a representative dataset and 3 canonical prompts that exercise edge regulatory cases. Emma, can you share those?
[02:57] Emma Rogers: Yes. We'll anonymize and send a 500-entry sample and 3 prompt templates. Want them by next week.
[03:05] Alice Chen: Great. We'll create a benchmark harness that measures latency, cost-per-call, token counts, and quality by running the samples and comparing to your ground truth labels.
[03:15] Mark Patel: For quality measurement, are you open to automated metrics plus a small human review set for ambiguous cases?
[03:21] Emma Rogers: Yes — automated pass/fail for redaction and a 100-case human check for borderline flags.
[03:28] Priya Rao: About security, we'll need SAML SSO + RBAC and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Also GDPR/data residency notes — our data must be processed in us-east-1.
[03:40] Alice Chen: We'll include SSO and RBAC in the plan; audit log forwarding is supported; we can pin region to us-east-1 for the Dedicated pool during the POC.
[03:50] Daniel Kim: Any limitations on KV cache or prefix caching for session reuse? We maintain session state for multi-turn clarifications.
[03:58] Mark Patel: Our runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching. For Dedicated we can get long-lived KV cache sessions with efficient eviction policies. There was a small note — sometimes transcripts auto-magically show K V cache in logs as two words — ignore that.
[04:14] Emma Rogers: (laughs) Noted.
[04:18] Alice Chen: Timeline — we suggest: kickoff week of Dec 27, access/setup completed in first week (VPC peering, service accounts, KMS), mid-point review at 3 weeks with initial benchmark results, and exec readout at 6 weeks. Does that align?
[04:33] Daniel Kim: That works for our exec calendar — we want the readout before mid-February.
[04:38] Priya Rao: Peering window — we need a 2-hour maintenance window during which Nova network team does the accept. We'll propose Jan 3 or Jan 4.
[04:48] Alice Chen: We'll flexible. We'll get a Redwood network engineer on the kickoff to coordinate. Mark, you'll own the infra handoff?
[04:55] Mark Patel: Yup, I'll run the handoff, provide the benchmark harness and the infra checklist: VPC CIDRs, peering steps, IAM roles, service account keys.
[05:05] Emma Rogers: On metrics, can you show token-level cost breakdown and p95/p99 latency per route?
[05:12] Mark Patel: Yes, our Console exposes token-level cost, per-route latency histograms, tracing and error analysis. We'll include screenshots in the pack.
[05:20] Daniel Kim: For cost targets — we need a comparison to our current on-prem setup. We'll send your team our billing/throughput numbers so you can calibrate the SOW estimate.
[05:30] Alice Chen: Perfect. We'll parameterize the SOW with your numbers.
[05:34] Emma Rogers: One question on fallbacks — if the Dedicated pool saturates, can requests route to a hosted fallback?
[05:41] Mark Patel: Yes, smart routing can fallback to a compatible hosted variant. We'll show you SLA tradeoffs in the report.
[05:48] Priya Rao: About logs — can Redwood redact PII before sending to third-party monitoring? We need the raw logs not to leave Nova control.
[05:57] Alice Chen: For Dedicated we can configure redaction rules and keep raw logs in a customer-owned S3 bucket if required. We'll document patterns.
[06:06] Daniel Kim: Ok, so to recap milestones and dates?
[06:10] Alice Chen: Kickoff: week of 2026-12-27. Access & infra handoff: by 2027-01-04. Mid-point benchmark review: 3 weeks after kickoff (~2027-01-17). Exec readout: 6 weeks after kickoff (~2027-02-07).
[06:26] Emma Rogers: Works. Are weekly syncs OK?
[06:29] Alice Chen: Yes — we'll do a short weekly sync and a dedicated mid-point deep-dive.
[06:34] Mark Patel: I'll also run an initial smoke test within 48 hours of access to validate connectivity and basic latency.
[06:41] Priya Rao: For SSO, we'll need SAML metadata and SP details. We'll send those to you.
[06:47] Alice Chen: Great. Action items we'll capture.
[06:50] [brief cross-talk as people confirm they can see the doc]
[07:05] Emma Rogers: One final technical ask: can you run the benchmark on both quantized and FP16 variants to show cost-performance tradeoffs?
[07:13] Mark Patel: Yes, we'll include a quantized profile and an FP16 baseline. We'll show quality delta vs cost.
[07:20] Daniel Kim: Also provide an ops runbook for scaling to production after POC — we might want Dedicated with autoscale rules.
[07:27] Alice Chen: We'll include recommended autoscale policies and burst capacity options in the SOW.
[07:33] Priya Rao: Feedback loop: if quality regresses during a rollout, we want automatic fallback to a known-good model and alert to our on-call. Can Redwood implement that?
[07:43] Mark Patel: Yes — rollback and automatic fallback policies are supported; we can tie alerts to your PagerDuty as well.
[07:51] Alice Chen: Ok, final recap of next steps now: I'll send security pack + SOC2 + draft SOW/pricing by Monday (2026-12-20). Mark will prepare the benchmark harness and infra checklist by 2026-12-22. Emma will share anonymized sample and prompts by 2026-12-22. Priya to confirm peering window and KMS requirements by 2026-12-23. We'll schedule kickoff for week of Dec 27.
[08:20] Emma Rogers: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[08:24] Daniel Kim: Thanks.
[08:26] Priya Rao: Thanks, bye.
